bull_bear.body: Prioritized: 1) project execution (Monte South Tower C, Nexzone Phase 3); 2) JDA/JV redevelopment in Central/South Mumbai; 3) FSI trading; 4) slum clearance infrastructure; no dividends or buybacks mentioned
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Slum clearance delays in Bhandup; environmental clearances for forest-adjacent plots; execution risk in large-scale township development; regulatory delays in Panvel 3.0 infrastructure rollout
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Highly confident and bullish; emphasized execution discipline, land bank value, infrastructure tailwinds (bullet train, airport, freeways), and QIP-funded acceleration; repeated use of 'strong', 'phenomenal', 'bright future'
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Marathon is quietly becoming a key enabler of Mumbai's slum rehabilitation via SRA cluster plans — leveraging its 50+ acre holdings to become a preferred partner for municipal redevelopment, not just a developer
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- "Completed Rs 900 crore QIP in June 2025, with Rs 340 crores earmarked for debt reduction" and "Achieved net cash position post-QIP, significantly strengthening balance sheet".
- Net debt chart shows Rs 838 Cr (FY23), Rs 751 Cr (FY24), Rs 542 Cr (FY25) and nil for both FY26 and FY27 Q1; the debt profile is described as "a conservative financial approach with a strong focus on maintaining low leverage, optimizing cost of capital, and ensuring ample liquidity".
- ~Rs 200+ Cr of acquisition capital is stated as available, with liquidity giving "the flexibility to pursue growth opportunities, accelerate project execution and enhance shareholder value".
- Expected surplus from ongoing projects is Rs 958 Cr on a 100% share basis and Rs 727 Cr on MNRL's share, against a cost to complete of Rs 1,461 Cr (100%) / Rs 928 Cr (MNRL share); OC-ready inventory adds Rs 247 Cr of surplus on MNRL's share.
- Growth has been acquisition-led: the milestone timeline lists purchases of Piramal Spinning & Weaving Mills (8 acres), 5.85 acres in Bhandup, 12.2 acres of Khatau Mills in Byculla, a JV stake in Futurex, Sanvo Resorts (25 acres in Panvel), Terrapolis Assets (1 acre in Mulund), Nexzone Fiscal Services (14 acres in Bhandup), controlling stakes in 3 real estate entities adding ~Rs 840 Cr of GDV potential, and a 90% stake in Sunset Spaces Pvt Ltd to strengthen the redevelopment pipeline.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- integration: in-house construction platform (MIVAN/Kumkang and PERI formwork, on-site batching plants, material testing laboratories, vertically integrated project management) with no dependence on external EPC contractors — evidence: 'The 65-storey towers at Monte South are being constructed entirely in-house'; 600+ professionals across the Group
- resource: land bank in MMR growth corridors — evidence: post-merger land bank of ~418 acres across Panvel (205 acres), Bhandup (130 acres) and Dombivli (83 acres) — against it: the land comes into the listed entity only through a merger that 'is subject to NCLT approval', and the timing of the final order 'remains subject to the regulatory process'
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Geographic concentration in the Mumbai Metropolitan Region — The company is active in only six MMR micro-markets (Byculla, Lower Parel, Panvel, Bhandup, Mulund, Dombivli). It argues each runs on its own demand and price cycle, but all its exposure is to one metropolitan region.
- Project execution risk — Several phased developments are under way, with ongoing projects between 52% and 91% complete, so construction timelines and revenue recognition depend on delivery.
- Dependence on public infrastructure in growth corridors — Part of the portfolio (Panvel, Bhandup) is in growth corridors whose appeal depends on active government infrastructure investment.
- Residential demand slowdown and demand-cycle volatility — The company names market slowdown and demand-cycle volatility as risks and relies on commercial assets and a mix of buyer profiles (luxury, mid-income, affordable) to cushion a residential downturn.
- Pipeline conversion / growth visibility — Growth depends on turning the announced pipeline (Rs 970 crores GDV: Nexzone Phase 3, NeoHomes) and Rs 7,792 crores of future-launch GDV (Monte South Commercial, Monte South Tower D, Neo Series) into launches.
- Construction input costs and energy-price volatility — The MD&A flags the rising cost of imported construction materials and global energy-price volatility, which it calls a key risk to the FY 2026-27 inflation outlook.
- Interest-rate environment — The MD&A names the higher-for-longer rate environment in advanced economies, which shapes global capital flows, as a main implication for real estate, though domestic home loan rates eased to 7.10-7.65% during the year.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Residential: Nexzone (Panvel, INR600cr GDV Phase 3), Neohomes (Bhandup, INR370cr GDV), Monte South (Bhandup, part OC for Tower B); Commercial: Futurex (strong tenant expansion), Monte South Commercial (JV with Adani, 7.5L sq.ft, INR3400cr GDV); Land Bank: 400+ acres across Bhandup (130ac), Panvel (205ac), Dombivli (80ac+)

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Self-described as a "Leading Mumbai-focused real estate developer with a diversified presence across key micro-markets", with ongoing projects at Panvel, Byculla, Lower Parel, Bhandup and Mulund.
- Growth is framed around six stated drivers: Amalgamation & Arrangement, strategically positioned land banks and dominance in key micro markets, strong liquidity, diversified portfolio for risk mitigation, and excellent in-house capabilities.
- Marathon Group (not the listed entity) credentials cited: established in 1978, 55+ years of experience, 100+ projects delivered, 10,000+ families housed, 15,000+ homes in the pipeline and 4 Mn sq.ft. of land under development.
- Monte South, Byculla is claimed to be "Among the top 5 projects in Byculla market by marketable supply", with 7.8 lakh sq. ft. (~Rs 2,403 Cr) sold to date.
- MNRL's own origin is stated as 2002 with the acquisition of Piramal Spinning & Weaving Mills Ltd (holding 8 acres of land) through the BIFR, rebranded as Marathon Nextgen Realty Limited in 2007.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Amalgamation] A scheme of Amalgamation & Arrangement would consolidate promoter and promoter-group assets into MNRL (the listed company); it has "Received 'No Adverse Observations' from BSE & NSE; Scheme now awaits NCLT approval" — i.e. it is not yet effective.
- [Merger impact on scale] Portfolio GDV moves from a pre-merger sub-total of Rs 18,792 Cr (unsold Rs 12,013 Cr; MNRL share of unsold Rs 7,606 Cr) to a post-merger total of Rs 20,751 Cr (unsold Rs 13,483 Cr; MNRL share of unsold Rs 8,723 Cr), with Futurex 2 (Rs 1,059 Cr) and Nextown (Rs 900 Cr) added.
- [Reporting basis] The deck reports Q1 FY27 operations on two bases in parallel — "Existing Portfolio" and "Merged Portfolio" — and states results are "Based on 40% share for Monte South project", with financial highlights noting inclusion of "actual sales value attributable to capital gains on FutureX inventory and 40% of Monte South turnover".
- [Partial ownership] Several assets are held below 100%: Monte South at 40%, Kanjurmarg acquisitions at 34% economic interest, Nexzone at 91%, NeoValley at 90%, Nextown at 59% and Marathon Ener-Gen LLP at 59.3%, so headline GDV and area figures diverge materially from MNRL's share.
- [Leadership] Promoter-family led: Chairman Chetan R. Shah (IIT Bombay, 40+ years), Vice Chairman Mayur R. Shah (30+ years, former President of MCHI-CREDAI), with next-generation directors heading specific projects (Nexzone/Futurex, Nexworld).
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: Marathon Nextgen Realty develops, constructs and sells residential and commercial real estate exclusively in the Mumbai Metropolitan Region, from ultra-luxury (Monte South) through mid-income (Nexzone) and mass affordable housing (NeoValley, NeoPark) to Grade A commercial developments (Futurex). It runs an in-house construction model with its own formwork systems, on-site batching plants and material testing laboratories, and sells through a custom CRM platform and a channel-partner network. It is also building a redevelopment platform in Mumbai, which now covers society redevelopment (Versova) and cluster redevelopment (Sewri).

outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: JDA/JV redevelopment in Central/South Mumbai using QIP funds; FSI trading to third-party builders; large-scale township development in Panvel and Dombivli; potential demerger of commercial assets post-stabilization
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- The company names four strategic pillars: strengthen the balance sheet, expand the development platform, simplify the corporate structure, and give better visibility of the next phase of growth.
- Merge promoter and promoter-group entities into the listed company under a Composite Scheme of Amalgamation. This would consolidate about 418 acres (130 acres in Bhandup, 83 in Dombivli, 205 in Panvel), part of the Futurex commercial portfolio and a few more projects. NSE and BSE have issued no-adverse-observation letters and the scheme is now before the NCLT.
- Keep a deliberately diversified portfolio across luxury residences, affordable housing, integrated townships, retail, Grade A commercial and small business spaces, so that no single segment, geography or demand cycle drives results.
- Run a sub-brand framework: 'Marathon Monte' for luxury residential, 'Marathon Nex' for townships in emerging growth corridors, and 'Marathon Neo' for aspirational, affordable homebuyers.
- Grow the pipeline through capital-efficient acquisitions on the Kanjurmarg model (controlling interest in three real estate entities). The same deal brought a B2B Permanent Transit Camp (PTC) vertical, which builds and sells transit accommodation units to other developers.
- Scale redevelopment: a 90% stake was bought in Sunset Spaces Private Limited, and several redevelopment projects are in advanced due diligence. They will be announced only once binding agreements are signed.
- Deploy QIP proceeds under a stated framework: debt repayment, faster construction on ongoing projects, and new project and land acquisitions.
- Manage risk structurally: keep the balance sheet debt-free, stay diversified, sequence launches around pre-sales, and be conservative about new land commitments.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Expansion here means buying projects and land, not building plants. In FY 2025-26 the company allocated Rs 160 crores of its Rs 900 crores QIP to speeding up construction on ongoing projects. It earmarked Rs 300 crores for future project acquisitions, part of which went into Kanjurmarg, and about Rs 250 crores remained available as of 31 March 2026. At Kanjurmarg it bought 51% controlling stakes in DVK Developers, Shree S S Developers and Shree Swami Samarth Builders for about Rs 70 crores, with a 34% economic interest. These add about 5.94 lakh sq. ft. of carpet area across six residential projects with an estimated GDV of over Rs 840 crores; part is under construction, several projects are expected to start within 12 months, and a large share will be built under the B2B Permanent Transit Camp (PTC) model. It also bought a 90% stake in Sunset Spaces Private Limited, which has since signed development agreements for a society redevelopment in Versova and a cluster redevelopment in Sewri, with a combined GDV of over Rs 900 crores. The proposed amalgamation, now before the NCLT after no-adverse-observation letters from BSE and NSE, would bring promoter-led entities owning more than 400 acres across Panvel, Bhandup and Dombivli into the listed company. Monte South Commercial, about 7.5 lakh sq. ft. of Grade A office and retail space in Byculla with a GDV of Rs 3,400 crores, has been announced and is moving towards launch.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- MMR infrastructure is expected to lift demand in the company's micro-markets. Navi Mumbai International Airport started commercial operations in December 2025 and now runs 24/7. The Mumbai Trans Harbour Link is operational, Goregaon-Mulund Link Road tunnelling is under way, and the Panvel-Karjat rail corridor and a planned High-Speed Rail station near Dombivli will support the company's land holdings.
- Industry consolidation: redevelopment opportunities and land deals are moving to organised, listed developers with stronger execution and balance sheets. New launches are expected to recover in FY 2026-27 as approvals improve.
- Luxury demand: Monte South pre-sales were driven by strong demand for luxury homes where supply at prime South Mumbai addresses is constrained.
- Grade A office demand: Futurex pre-sales grew on continued demand for Grade A office space. GCCs account for over one third of net office absorption, and MMR recorded a 2.6x demand-to-supply ratio with 11.7% vacancy.
- Rates and affordability: the RBI cut the repo rate by 125 bps to 5.25% by December 2025 and home loan rates eased to 7.10-7.65%, improving affordability. Global energy-price volatility remains a risk to the FY 2026-27 inflation outlook.
- Airport and infrastructure development lifted Nexzone (Panvel) pre-sales, and better connectivity along the Eastern Express Highway supported the Neo series (Bhandup).
- Named headwinds: global macroeconomic uncertainty, interest-rate trajectories and home-loan affordability, changing regulation, possible demand-supply imbalances in select micro-markets, and uncertainty over the pace of infrastructure delivery in peripheral areas.
- Current unsold GDV stands at over Rs 6,400 crores. The Kanjurmarg acquisition adds a further Rs 280-300 crores of GDV potential, taking the visible pipeline to well over Rs 6,700 crores before the post-merger land bank.
- Kanjurmarg: three entities hold six residential projects with an estimated GDV above Rs 840 crores. One is under construction (structural work at the fifth slab of a 23-storey tower), and more than Rs 225 crores of GDV is expected to launch within the next 12 months.
- Project pre-sales in FY 2025-26: Marathon Futurex Rs 466 crores (combined post-merger basis, up 15% YoY), Monte South Rs 391 crores, Marathon Nexzone Rs 104 crores, Neo series Rs 65 crores, Marathon Millennium Rs 21 crores.
- The company says it enters FY 2026-27 with its strongest-ever pipeline of committed, launched and near-launch projects.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Marathon delivered record H1 PAT of INR128cr (+47% YoY) driven by strong sales velocity in Futurex, Monte South, and Nexzone, with a robust launch pipeline and QIP-funded capital to accelerate monetization of its 400+ acre land bank across high-growth Mumbai micro-markets.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Mumbai Metropolitan Region-only real estate developer spanning luxury, mid-income and affordable housing and Grade A commercial space, with a post-merger land bank of about 418 acres.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Marathon Nextgen Realty develops, constructs and sells residential and commercial real estate exclusively in the Mumbai Metropolitan Region, from ultra-luxury (Monte South) through mid-income (Nexzone) and mass affordable housing (NeoValley, NeoPark) to Grade A commercial developments (Futurex). It runs an in-house construction model with its own formwork systems, on-site batching plants and material testing laboratories, and sells through a custom CRM platform and a channel-partner network. It is also building a redevelopment platform in Mumbai, which now covers society redevelopment (Versova) and cluster redevelopment (Sewri).

group_structure.title: Group structure (profile)
group_structure.body:
- Marathon Realty Private Limited — related party: Holding company (BRSR item 23). AOC-2 counterparty for loans. The FY26 AGM notice seeks shareholder approval for a material related-party transaction with it (loans/advances/securities).
- Terrapolis Assets Private Limited — subsidiary: 100% held; described as a material and wholly owned subsidiary in AOC-2 (loans/receivables)
- Sanvo Resorts Private Limited — subsidiary: 91% held; material subsidiary per AOC-2 (loans/receivables/payable)
- Nexzone Fiscal Services Private Limited — subsidiary: 90% held; AOC-2 counterparty (loans/receivables/payable)
- Marathon Nexzone Land Private Limited — subsidiary: 100% held
- Marathon Energy Private Limited — subsidiary: 100% held
- Kanchi Rehab Private Limited — subsidiary: 100% held
- Nexzone IT Infrastructure Private Limited — subsidiary: 100% held
- Nexzone Water Management Private Limited — subsidiary: 100% held
- Sunset Spaces Private Limited — subsidiary: 90% held; subsidiary since 09 March 2026; AOC-2 counterparty (loans)
- Swayam Realtors And Traders LLP — JV: Joint venture, 40% held; AOC-2 counterparty (loans/receivables)
- Columbia Chrome (India) Private Limited — JV: Joint venture, 40% held

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: Residential: Nexzone (Panvel, INR600cr GDV Phase 3), Neohomes (Bhandup, INR370cr GDV), Monte South (Bhandup, part OC for Tower B); Commercial: Futurex (strong tenant expansion), Monte South Commercial (JV with Adani, 7.5L sq.ft, INR3400cr GDV); Land Bank: 400+ acres across Bhandup (130ac), Panvel (205ac), Dombivli (80ac+)

end_markets.body:

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: JDA/JV redevelopment in Central/South Mumbai using QIP funds; FSI trading to third-party builders; large-scale township development in Panvel and Dombivli; potential demerger of commercial assets post-stabilization

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- MMR infrastructure is expected to lift demand in the company's micro-markets. Navi Mumbai International Airport started commercial operations in December 2025 and now runs 24/7. The Mumbai Trans Harbour Link is operational, Goregaon-Mulund Link Road tunnelling is under way, and the Panvel-Karjat rail corridor and a planned High-Speed Rail station near Dombivli will support the company's land holdings.
- Industry consolidation: redevelopment opportunities and land deals are moving to organised, listed developers with stronger execution and balance sheets. New launches are expected to recover in FY 2026-27 as approvals improve.
- Luxury demand: Monte South pre-sales were driven by strong demand for luxury homes where supply at prime South Mumbai addresses is constrained.
- Grade A office demand: Futurex pre-sales grew on continued demand for Grade A office space. GCCs account for over one third of net office absorption, and MMR recorded a 2.6x demand-to-supply ratio with 11.7% vacancy.
- Rates and affordability: the RBI cut the repo rate by 125 bps to 5.25% by December 2025 and home loan rates eased to 7.10-7.65%, improving affordability. Global energy-price volatility remains a risk to the FY 2026-27 inflation outlook.
- Airport and infrastructure development lifted Nexzone (Panvel) pre-sales, and better connectivity along the Eastern Express Highway supported the Neo series (Bhandup).
- Named headwinds: global macroeconomic uncertainty, interest-rate trajectories and home-loan affordability, changing regulation, possible demand-supply imbalances in select micro-markets, and uncertainty over the pace of infrastructure delivery in peripheral areas.
- Current unsold GDV stands at over Rs 6,400 crores. The Kanjurmarg acquisition adds a further Rs 280-300 crores of GDV potential, taking the visible pipeline to well over Rs 6,700 crores before the post-merger land bank.
- Kanjurmarg: three entities hold six residential projects with an estimated GDV above Rs 840 crores. One is under construction (structural work at the fifth slab of a 23-storey tower), and more than Rs 225 crores of GDV is expected to launch within the next 12 months.
- Project pre-sales in FY 2025-26: Marathon Futurex Rs 466 crores (combined post-merger basis, up 15% YoY), Monte South Rs 391 crores, Marathon Nexzone Rs 104 crores, Neo series Rs 65 crores, Marathon Millennium Rs 21 crores.
- The company says it enters FY 2026-27 with its strongest-ever pipeline of committed, launched and near-launch projects.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Margins improving via premium mix (Monte South, Futurex), FSI trading (Bhandup), and in-house execution; cost discipline maintained; no inflationary pressure cited; rental yields rising in commercial assets

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Prioritized: 1) project execution (Monte South Tower C, Nexzone Phase 3); 2) JDA/JV redevelopment in Central/South Mumbai; 3) FSI trading; 4) slum clearance infrastructure; no dividends or buybacks mentioned

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Expansion here means buying projects and land, not building plants. In FY 2025-26 the company allocated Rs 160 crores of its Rs 900 crores QIP to speeding up construction on ongoing projects. It earmarked Rs 300 crores for future project acquisitions, part of which went into Kanjurmarg, and about Rs 250 crores remained available as of 31 March 2026. At Kanjurmarg it bought 51% controlling stakes in DVK Developers, Shree S S Developers and Shree Swami Samarth Builders for about Rs 70 crores, with a 34% economic interest. These add about 5.94 lakh sq. ft. of carpet area across six residential projects with an estimated GDV of over Rs 840 crores; part is under construction, several projects are expected to start within 12 months, and a large share will be built under the B2B Permanent Transit Camp (PTC) model. It also bought a 90% stake in Sunset Spaces Private Limited, which has since signed development agreements for a society redevelopment in Versova and a cluster redevelopment in Sewri, with a combined GDV of over Rs 900 crores. The proposed amalgamation, now before the NCLT after no-adverse-observation letters from BSE and NSE, would bring promoter-led entities owning more than 400 acres across Panvel, Bhandup and Dombivli into the listed company. Monte South Commercial, about 7.5 lakh sq. ft. of Grade A office and retail space in Byculla with a GDV of Rs 3,400 crores, has been announced and is moving towards launch.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Highly confident and bullish; emphasized execution discipline, land bank value, infrastructure tailwinds (bullet train, airport, freeways), and QIP-funded acceleration; repeated use of 'strong', 'phenomenal', 'bright future'

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- integration: in-house construction platform (MIVAN/Kumkang and PERI formwork, on-site batching plants, material testing laboratories, vertically integrated project management) with no dependence on external EPC contractors — evidence: 'The 65-storey towers at Monte South are being constructed entirely in-house'; 600+ professionals across the Group
- resource: land bank in MMR growth corridors — evidence: post-merger land bank of ~418 acres across Panvel (205 acres), Bhandup (130 acres) and Dombivli (83 acres) — against it: the land comes into the listed entity only through a merger that 'is subject to NCLT approval', and the timing of the final order 'remains subject to the regulatory process'

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Slum clearance delays in Bhandup; environmental clearances for forest-adjacent plots; execution risk in large-scale township development; regulatory delays in Panvel 3.0 infrastructure rollout

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Marathon is quietly becoming a key enabler of Mumbai's slum rehabilitation via SRA cluster plans — leveraging its 50+ acre holdings to become a preferred partner for municipal redevelopment, not just a developer

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- The company names four strategic pillars: strengthen the balance sheet, expand the development platform, simplify the corporate structure, and give better visibility of the next phase of growth.
- Merge promoter and promoter-group entities into the listed company under a Composite Scheme of Amalgamation. This would consolidate about 418 acres (130 acres in Bhandup, 83 in Dombivli, 205 in Panvel), part of the Futurex commercial portfolio and a few more projects. NSE and BSE have issued no-adverse-observation letters and the scheme is now before the NCLT.
- Keep a deliberately diversified portfolio …

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Amalgamation] A scheme of Amalgamation & Arrangement would consolidate promoter and promoter-group assets into MNRL (the listed company); it has "Received 'No Adverse Observations' from BSE & NSE; Scheme now awaits NCLT approval" — i.e. it is not yet effective.
- [Merger impact on scale] Portfolio GDV moves from a pre-merger sub-total of Rs 18,792 Cr (unsold Rs 12,013 Cr; MNRL share of unsold Rs 7,606 Cr) to a post-merger total of Rs 20,751 Cr (unsold Rs 13,483 Cr; MNRL share of unsold Rs 8,723 Cr), with Futurex 2 (Rs 1,059 Cr) and Nextown (Rs 900 Cr) added.
- [Reporting basis] The deck reports Q1 FY27 operations on two bases in parallel — "Existing Portfolio" and "Merged Portfolio" — and states results are "Based on 40% share for Monte South project", with financial highlights noting inclusion of "actual sales value attributable to capital gains on FutureX inventory and 40% of Monte South turnover".
- [Partial ownership] Several assets are held below 100%: Monte South at 40%, Kanjurmarg acquisitions at 34% economic interest, Nexzone at 91%, NeoValley at 90%, Nextown at 59% and Marathon Ener-Gen LLP at 59.3%, so headline GDV and area figures diverge materially from MNRL's share.
- [Leadership] Promoter-family led: Chairman Chetan R. Shah (IIT Bombay, 40+ years), Vice Chairman Mayur R. Shah (30+ years, former President of MCHI-CREDAI), with next-generation directors heading specific projects (Nexzone/Futurex, Nexworld).

themes.title: Real-estate up-cycle - premium housing & redevelopment
themes.need: The residential up-cycle is now presales-led with a visible margin cost. SOBHA posted its highest-ever presales at INR 3,656cr (+76% YoY, 2.34 msf at an average INR 15,655/sqft, NCR at a record INR 1,384cr) and guided FY27 presales at +30% or better - but reported EBITDA is still only ~9.7%, guided to 17-20% only by exit-Q4, and forthcoming-project marginal cash flow was cut from ~INR 86bn to INR 68.3bn on a heavier joint-development mix. SUNTECK booked INR 787cr of presales (+20%) with ZERO launches in the quarter, with aspirational-luxury (Naigaon/Kalyan) at 21% of presales 'picking up because of the lower interest rate' - the first sign the rate-elastic end is turning on demand rather than inventory release. DLF's FY26 bookings of INR20,143cr and 50mn sq ft of rental at 95% occupancy anchor the annuity leg; LODHA/GODREJPROP/PRESTIGE-tier and MMR redevelopers (RUSTOMJEE, KALPATARU, RAYMONDREL, MANINFRA, SURAJEST) ride premiumization; PHOENIXLTD/EMBDL on mixed-use.
themes.driver: SOBHA's exit-Q4 margin ramp from ~9.7% to 17-20% is the falsifiable claim (JD-heavy growth structurally lowers marginal margins); rate-elastic aspirational absorption (SUNTECK); FY27 launch-pipeline execution and festive booking momentum.
